scope: Native browser encoding/playback and private local audio workflows with synthetic input; not physical-device or speech-service acceptance

environment.microphone_input: Synthetic Web Audio oscillator routed only to a MediaStream destination, not to physical speakers

backend.scope: All import, audio API and hosted tests, including both consumers of the extracted shared WAV fixture; not the full repository Python suite.
backend.note: Existing dependency deprecation and expected injected-failure logs were printed; all tests passed.

frontend_unit.scope: Recorder lifecycle, denial/disconnection/size errors, audio focus, attachment review and consent with unit-test media fixtures.

mocked_browsers.scope: Existing desktop/mobile synthetic recording and microphone-denial cases after extracting the shared browser microphone setup. API responses are mocked in this layer.

live_browsers.scope: Entire current live suite: five scenarios on two profiles. Audio checks reuse existing synthetic accounts to stay within the unchanged registration throttle.
scenarios: Registration, verification, private terminology/audio, sessions and reload persistence
Saved dictionary translation, projects, revisions and verified backup restoration
Password recovery, old-session revocation and replacement password
Six local document formats, corrected draft handoff and explicit unreviewed saving
Document limits/errors and audio permission, attachment, recording lifecycle and consent

initial_live_run.reason: The newly added playback-pause assertion searched through a visible-only article locator after navigation deliberately hid that page. Trace output confirmed locator.evaluate was waiting for the hidden ancestor, not observing an unpaused player.
initial_live_run.correction: Find the unique audio element by its exact accessible label so the hidden player remains addressable; assert it exists, then inspect its paused state.

validation.editor_diagnostics: No errors in changed Python/TypeScript files
validation.python_fixture_signature: All five wav_bytes call sites remain compatible after extraction.

owner_hardware_follow_up.approved_action: Record and play a 5-10 second local draft saying Mboa audio test, one two three; no upload or AI processing.
owner_hardware_follow_up.owner_initial_report: This recording could not be played. It may be missing, damaged or unsupported by this browser. Download it to check with another player.
owner_hardware_follow_up.owner_clarification: Yes—Chrome/Edge work; only VS Code fails
owner_hardware_follow_up.scope: Human confirmation of physical microphone and audible playback in normal browsers; not browser dictation, read-aloud, physical-mobile or cloud-transcription acceptance.

vscode_embedded_browser_follow_up.probe: Created an independent synthetic Web Audio oscillator/MediaStream, encoded 1.2 seconds with the native MediaRecorder, and attempted muted playback of the resulting browser blob in a new Audio element. No app recorder or provider API was called.
vscode_embedded_browser_follow_up.exception_message: Failed to load because no supported source was found.
vscode_embedded_browser_follow_up.conclusion: The owner's editor-only failure is reproducible in the embedded media pipeline, independently of Mboa recording UI and server audio storage. The exact underlying editor/FFmpeg cause is not established; do not change the app's default recording format based only on the advertised codec support.
vscode_embedded_browser_follow_up.workaround: Use the owner-confirmed working Chrome/Edge browsers for recording and audible playback.

limitations: The automated suite used no human speech or physical devices. Normal-browser physical recording/playback was subsequently owner-confirmed, not independently observed; the two evidence types are distinguished above.
WebM and PCM WAV were exercised with real browser bytes; every browser, operating system and advertised attachment codec was not tested.
Browser dictation and text-to-speech depend on the user's browser, permissions, installed voices and possibly browser-provider services; this run does not certify them.
Gemini audio/video transcription, cloud OCR, assistant responses and the remaining AI translation directions are still unverified.
Mobile emulation is not acceptance on a physical mobile device or with assistive technology.
These local, uncommitted changes do not establish Ubuntu VPS readiness, a complete green remote CI run or public-deployment approval.
